title: 2.1 Conditional Statements

icans: I can identify the hypothesis and conclusion of a conditional statement.
I can write the converse, inverse, and contrapositive and decide whether each is true.
I can write a biconditional statement.

vocab: a logical statement with a _____________ and a conclusion, written “if p, then q”
the statement formed by switching the _____________ and the conclusion
the statement formed by negating both the _____________ and the conclusion
the statement formed by switching and negating the _____________ and the conclusion
a statement that ___________ the phrase “if and only if”

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Discovery: true one way, false the other?

blocks.p: Is each statement true? Switch the “if” and “then” parts. Is it still true?

head: Statement
True?
Switched
True?
rows: If an animal is a dog, then it has four legs.
If an angle measures 90°, then it is a right angle.
If a number is even, then it ends in 4.

blocks.p: One example that shows a statement is false is called a ______________.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Conditional statement: “if p, then q”; p is the _______________ and q is the _______________.

blocks.stem: Identify the hypothesis and the conclusion: “If a polygon has 5 sides, then it is a pentagon.”
Rewrite in if-then form: “All 90° angles are right angles.”

notes: Related conditionals: converse q → p, inverse ~p → ~q, contrapositive _______________. A conditional and its _______________ are always both true or both false.

blocks.stem: Write the converse, inverse, and contrapositive of “If two angles form a linear pair, then they are supplementary.” Decide whether each is true.
Is the statement true? If not, give a counterexample: “If x² = 16, then x = 4.”

notes: Biconditional: when a conditional and its converse are both true, combine them with the words _______________.

blocks.stem: Write as a biconditional: “If two lines intersect to form a right angle, then they are perpendicular.” (Its converse is also true.)
Write the converse of “If a figure is a square, then it has four sides.” Is the converse true?
Write the contrapositive of “If m∠A = 30°, then ∠A is acute.” Is it true?

tickets.stem: What is the hypothesis of “If you study, then you will pass”?
Write the converse of “If a number is even, then it is divisible by 2.”
Give a counterexample: “If an angle is acute, then it measures 45°.”
